questions.question: What is a mock object in Mockito?
options: A fake copy of a class whose answers you control and whose calls you can check
A copy of the production database
A faster version of the JVM
A second copy of the test class
questions.explanation: A mock stands in for a real helper, so a test can control what it returns and verify how it was called.

questions.question: What is the difference between @Mock and @MockitoBean?
options: There is none, they are aliases
@Mock is plain Mockito, @MockitoBean puts a mock into the Spring context
questions.explanation: @Mock creates a mock for a plain unit test, while @MockitoBean replaces a bean inside the Spring application context.

questions.question: A test stubs gateway.charge("Meera", 450) to return false, then calls placeOrder. The code sends an SMS only when the charge works. What does verify(sms, never()).send(anyString(), anyString()) do?
options: Fails, because the SMS was sent
Passes, because no SMS was sent
questions.explanation: The payment failed, so the code never called send, and verify with never() passes.

questions.question: A mock method that returns int is called without any stubbing. What does it return?
questions.explanation: Mockito returns default values for unstubbed calls: 0 for numbers, false for booleans and null for objects.

questions.question: A test class uses @Mock and @InjectMocks but has no @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class). The test fails with a NullPointerException. Why?
options: Mocks are never created, so the fields stay null
The test method must be static
questions.explanation: Without the extension nobody processes the annotations, so the mock and injected fields remain null.
